lessons.title: The contact center is not the whole operation
lessons.why: WFM, quality, emergency location, and the CRM fail quietly when they are bolted on after go-live.
paras: Connect owns the live contact. Forecasting and scheduling own the shift. Recording and evaluations own the proof. Profiles and the CRM own the person. E911 owns the agent's location during a 911 call. AI assist owns a recommendation, not the decision.
The mind map in this track is the picture you put on the wall. The glossary is the dictionary that stops two teams using 'queue' for six different objects.
points: Every sister system must store ContactId or it cannot be audited.
Pick one system of record for the case.
Pick one adherence feed: agent events.
Pick one emergency design per kind of agent: desk phone or CCP.
lessons.mistake: A go-live checklist that ends at 'agent answered a call'.

number.n: Contact, shift, proof, person, location, recommendation

lessons.title: Glossary
lessons.why: A migration argument is usually two definitions of the same word.
paras: This lesson is the glossary. Search it. Each term has a one- or two-sentence meaning and a source. Prefer these meanings in design reviews. If a vendor uses the word differently, write their meaning next to it rather than overloading the word.
Start with contact, queue, routing profile, attribute, CTR, and ContactId. Then add the sister-system words: adherence, evaluation, civic address, and screen pop.
points: The glossary is also a flashcard deck.
Old-platform words are included on purpose.
Ended features stay in the glossary so people can see the date.
If a definition has no source, it does not belong here.
lessons.mistake: A project wiki that redefines 'skill' every quarter.

lessons.title: Mind map
lessons.why: If you cannot point at the box that owns a function, you will build it twice.
paras: The center is the contact. Around it: telephony, flows, routing, the CCP, profiles and cases, conversational analytics, WFM, recording, the CRM, E911, and agent assist. Lines are keys, not vibes: ContactId, profile id, agent event, civic address, S3 object.
Click a node in the lab. The panel says what you configure, what breaks, and which hook a future system should use.
points: Telephony is not the CRM.
WFM is not the real-time board.
E911 is not the customer's caller ID.
Agent assist is not the system of record.
lessons.mistake: A diagram that is only logos.

lessons.title: Native forecasting and scheduling
lessons.why: Native WFM is in the product. Third-party WFM is justified when you already live in that suite, not because Connect 'cannot schedule'.
paras: Forecasting predicts volume and handle time and refreshes intraday every 15 minutes. Capacity planning turns that into people, using service level and shrinkage. Scheduling publishes shifts from skills, patterns, and rules. Adherence metrics exist after you publish.
The 4 August 2026 rename is forecasting and agent scheduling. Agents see shifts in the workspace. Time-off rules are not hours of operation.
points: You need history before the forecast is trustworthy.
Shrinkage is an input you own. The tool does not know your meetings.
Published schedules are what adherence compares against.
A queue with no staffable profile makes the forecast look 'wrong'.
lessons.mistake: Buying a second WFM and also turning on native scheduling for the same team.

lessons.title: Third-party WFM configuration and faults
lessons.why: The integration is the agent event stream plus a historical extract. If either is late, adherence is fiction.
paras: Aspect's deployment uses one agent-event stream, optionally Firehose into S3, and scheduled report exports. Eleveo describes the same pair: agent events for the live listener, CTRs and recordings for history. Both need a status map.
Faults: one shard and two consumers, a status renamed in Connect and not in the WFM tool, a missed logout, and a schedule that was never published so adherence is blank.
points: Give each consumer its own iterator.
Alarm on iterator age.
Map statuses in a reviewed table.
Do not send production events into a vendor lab account.
lessons.mistake: A VPN from the WFM server into the CCP as the 'integration'.

number.n: Agent events, sized for every consumer

lessons.title: Recording and screen capture
lessons.why: If the object is not in S3, you do not have a recording, no matter what the flow block said.
paras: Set the recording and analytics block on the contact, including outbound whisper flows if outbound must be recorded. The service role writes the WAV. The CTR carries the location. Screen recording is a separate decision and, on the Basic list, 0.006 USD per minute.
Tell people they are recorded if the law you operate under says so. The prompt is a block, not a policy PDF.
points: Customer and agent channels should be identifiable for QM.
KMS failures look like missing files.
A transfer to the PSTN ends Connect's recording of the far leg.
Retention is a lifecycle rule you write down.
lessons.mistake: Recording only the inbound flow and wondering why outbound disputes have no audio.

lessons.title: Third-party recorders and live media
lessons.why: Some QM suites want the audio while the call is up. That is Kinesis Video Streams, not a second SIP trunk.
paras: Start media streaming opens live customer audio. Stop media streaming ends it. Third-party tools consume the stream. A tool in another account needs the stream ARN from the contact event and an IAM role that can read it. After the call, many tools also import the WAV from S3 using the CTR.

Faults: streaming never started because the block was skipped, the cross-account role is wrong, or the tool looks for a stereo file Connect did not write in the shape it expects. Read the tool's format note. Do not guess PCM layout.
points: Streaming and S3 recording can both be on. Know which one the evaluator uses.
Stop the stream. Leaked streams cost money and keep audio you meant to end.
Do not stream calls that your policy says must not be recorded.
Test cross-account access with a security review, not with a long-lived access key.
lessons.mistake: Mirroring the RTP to a recorder VM on a shelf.

flow.label: Import
flow.detail: WAV later if the tool wants a file.

lessons.title: Quality management on top of analytics
lessons.why: A score without the recording is an opinion. A recording without a form is an archive.
paras: Evaluation forms were previewed 29 November 2022 and became generally available 26 April 2023. They sit with conversational analytics. You can score a contact, calibrate reviewers, and coach. Generative scoring, where you turn it on, is still a score someone must be willing to defend.
The quota table limits how many evaluation questions AI may answer on one contact. Read that limit before you design a 40-question form and assume a model fills it.
points: Calibrate reviewers on the same five contacts.
The transcript can miss a word. The audio decides.
Redaction must run before a reviewer who should not see the secret sees the form.
Coaching is a workflow. The form is not the coaching.
lessons.mistake: Auto-failing an agent on a summary that paraphrased badly.

lessons.title: Configure conversational analytics and fix the empty transcript
lessons.why: Analytics that is not enabled on the contact produces an empty search and a false 'the feature is down'.
paras: Enable the analytics behavior on the recording block for the flows that need it, including the outbound whisper if outbound matters. Confirm the language. Confirm redaction. Check the real-time quota if supervisors say rules never fire during a storm. Post-call jobs scale with minutes. Use the quota page's 40 percent rule of thumb to see if you are out of job concurrency.
Names: the console may say conversational analytics. Your old diagram may say Contact Lens. Search both.
points: A flow that sets recording off 'for this queue' also kills the transcript.
Rules on keywords need the real-time path.
Summaries are absent until the post-contact job finishes.
Chat analytics is a separate enablement from voice. It arrived later and is configured on the chat contact.
lessons.mistake: Opening a support case for 'Contact Lens missing' on a flow that never set the block.

number.n: Of call length, for post-call job concurrency

lessons.title: E911 for agents on the CCP
lessons.why: A contact-center platform is not automatically an emergency-calling design. In the US Regions where this exists, you still have to store a real address.
paras: Direct 911 from the CCP is enabled by default in US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), and GovCloud US-West. Connect does not transfer a live call to 911 and does not let an agent dial 911 while already on a call. E911 sends a validated physical address. You validate with the Chime ValidateE911Address API, store it on the agent's Customer Profile, and an outbound whisper flow copies it to the CivicAddress attribute when the dialed string is 911.

Test with 933. It reads back the number and the address. The docs describe a 100 USD penalty for a non-emergency 911 call. The origination number must be callable if responders need to ring back. Create a task in that whisper flow so security is notified. Home agents must update the address when they move. A CUCM ELIN for the office does not cover them.
points: CivicAddress is a JSON string, not a JSON object. The keys include country, A1, A3, HNO, RD, STS, and PC.
Prompt agents to confirm the address at the start of a shift if they roam.
This is not available as a transfer from a customer call.
Outside those Regions, do not invent a 911 design. Use the local emergency method and say so.
lessons.mistake: Telling home agents to dial 911 on the CCP while the stored address is the headquarters.

flow.label: Whisper
flow.detail: If the dial string is 911 or 933.

lessons.title: CRM configuration and the faults that look like routing bugs
lessons.why: A wrong screen pop is often an attribute bug, not a Salesforce bug.
paras: Salesforce: sandbox, package, CCP embed or SCC-AC, one case owner, click-to-dial. ServiceNow: imported flows, queue map, hold file under 5 seconds, one router. Both need the customer id written before the agent is offered the contact.

Faults: pop on the wrong record because ANI matched a household, a blank pop because the attribute name does not match the softphone layout, a double agent because AWA and Connect both routed, and a transfer to CUCM that strands the CRM because the second leg has no ContactId.
points: Log the attribute in the flow and in the CRM activity.
Search profiles before creating a lead.
Outbound click-to-dial uses the queue caller ID.
Retest after every managed-package upgrade in a sandbox.
lessons.mistake: Opening the CRM with a hard-coded account so the demo works.

flow.label: Transfer
flow.detail: Know when the id will vanish.

lessons.title: AI agents: configure, cite, and a way out
lessons.why: An agent who cannot reach a person is not assisted. They are stuck.
paras: Attach the domain with the Connect assistant block only on flows where the knowledge base has an owner. For self-service, the Agentic CX exit conditions must include failure and 'human'. External Tool calls need a permission review. Live Sync is optional and priced.

Faults: empty recommendations because the block never ran, answers from a stale article, a policy written for the wrong IAM prefix, and a bot that consumes the 8-second Lambda budget inside a tool call.
points: Every generated answer in a design review needs the article title.
Keep DTMF escape.
Do not send payment card data into a prompt.
Voice ID is not the fallback. It has ended.
lessons.mistake: Turning on generative self-service for the main number on day one.

lessons.title: Integration maps
lessons.why: A map is a list of seams with a key on each line. A poster of logos is not a map.
paras: Seam examples this campus will draw in the lab: Salesforce embed, ServiceNow queue map, Teams chat, CUCM transfer, WFM agent events, QM via S3 or KVS, E911 whisper, analytics stream. Each row has a producer, a consumer, a key, a protocol, and the first fault to check.
If you cannot name the key, you are not ready to build the seam.
points: ContactId joins contact-scoped tools.
Profile id joins customer-scoped tools.
Agent ARN or username joins WFM.
CivicAddress joins only the 911 whisper.

number.n: Producer, consumer, key, protocol, first fault

lessons.title: Future hooks, not future rewrites
lessons.why: Add the next system on a hook that already exists. Do not scrape the CCP and do not fork the flow for every vendor.
paras: Hooks you can adopt later: EventBridge contact events, the CTR stream, agent events, Kinesis Video, Customer Profiles events, Cases, Show view, data tables, External Tool, and the flow language JSON in your pipeline. Live Sync and Agentic CX are the 2026 hooks for guided and agentic experiences.
A hook has a schema and a permission. Write both down when you 'leave room' for a vendor. Room without a schema is a hope.
points: Prefer events over polling the real-time API.
Prefer attributes over asking the agent to retype.
Prefer a module for a policy that every future flow must share.
Re-read the quota before you promise a vendor a fan-out.
lessons.mistake: A custom browser extension that clicks the CCP.

number.n: Events, streams, views, tables, tools, modules
